k: _one in the fen and one in the wood, / one where the storm-winds wander, / and one in the City of Bells, my love — / and the dark on the other side, yonder._
src: '_one in the fen and one in the wood, / one where the storm-winds wander, / and one in the City of Bells, my love — / and the dark on the other side, yonder._'

k: Old fen song. Older than the Choir. My gran sang the last verse different.
src: 'Old fen song. Older than the Choir. My gran sang the last verse different.'

k: Different how?
src: 'Different how?'

k: "_And one in the City of Bells, my love, that went out once — and grew fonder._"
src: '"_And one in the City of Bells, my love, that went out once — and grew fonder._"'

k: Never understood it. Nice rhyme, though.
src: 'Never understood it. Nice rhyme, though.'

k: Twenty-four patients. Twenty-four draughts. The girl brewed them all and then fell asleep standing up.
src: 'Twenty-four patients. Twenty-four draughts. The girl brewed them all and then fell asleep standing up.'

k: Thirty years a doctor, and a sixteen-year-old taught me something. I'm going to go and be humbled somewhere private.
src: 'Thirty years a doctor, and a sixteen-year-old taught me something. I\'m going to go and be humbled somewhere private.'

k: Take these. I won't need them now. Well — I will. Take them anyway.
src: 'Take these. I won\'t need them now. Well — I will. Take them anyway.'

k: I've written her recipe on the inside of my sleeve. I'm never washing this coat again.
src: 'I\'ve written her recipe on the inside of my sleeve. I\'m never washing this coat again.'

k: If the girl can really make the Marrow remedy, she'll want my mortar. It's the one that isn't cracked.
src: 'If the girl can really make the Marrow remedy, she\'ll want my mortar. It\'s the one that isn\'t cracked.'

k: ...Less cracked.
src: '...Less cracked.'

k: The Rot House. Twenty beds. Twenty-four patients. I've stopped being good at sums.
src: 'The Rot House. Twenty beds. Twenty-four patients. I\'ve stopped being good at sums.'

k: Don't touch anyone's hands. Don't breathe near the coughing ones. Don't, on the whole, be here.
src: 'Don\'t touch anyone\'s hands. Don\'t breathe near the coughing ones. Don\'t, on the whole, be here.'

k: I wrote to the Cathedral. I told them the Rot House is empty and asked them to send Mirefen's stone home.
src: 'I wrote to the Cathedral. I told them the Rot House is empty and asked them to send Mirefen\'s stone home.'

k: They haven't answered. They always answer.
src: 'They haven\'t answered. They always answer.'

k: ...I'm going back on the next barge. I'm going to ask in person.
src: '...I\'m going back on the next barge. I\'m going to ask in person.'

k: I came on the Cathedral's barge to tend the sick. When it left, I stayed.
src: 'I came on the Cathedral\'s barge to tend the sick. When it left, I stayed.'

k: His Grace took the Dawnstone to keep it safe. The Gloam is rising everywhere. Better the stones rest in the Cathedral than be lost.
src: 'His Grace took the Dawnstone to keep it safe. The Gloam is rising everywhere. Better the stones rest in the Cathedral than be lost.'

k: That's what I was told. That's what I believe.
src: 'That\'s what I was told. That\'s what I believe.'

k: Please don't look at me like that.
src: 'Please don\'t look at me like that.'

k: ...You. The girl with the black hair. Have we met?
src: '...You. The girl with the black hair. Have we met?'

k: I do not think so.
src: 'I do not think so.'

k: I know your face. From a painting, I think. In the Cathedral — above the door of His Grace's private chapel.
src: 'I know your face. From a painting, I think. In the Cathedral — above the door of His Grace\'s private chapel.'

k: A little girl, holding a lantern. The Hierophant lights a candle under it every morning.
src: 'A little girl, holding a lantern. The Hierophant lights a candle under it every morning.'

k: "—four for the eel and five for the frog, six for the Keeper who sings through the fog!"
src: '"—four for the eel and five for the frog, six for the Keeper who sings through the fog!"'

k: I can say the whole thing now! The Mender-girl made me drink a boot.
src: 'I can say the whole thing now! The Mender-girl made me drink a boot.'

k: There is no seven.
src: 'There is no seven.'

k: Seven's for you. You choose what it's for. That's the rule.
src: 'Seven\'s for you. You choose what it\'s for. That\'s the rule.'

k: ...I will think about it carefully.
src: '...I will think about it carefully.'

k: I'm not scared. Mother Osk says the rot is just the dark being rude.
src: 'I\'m not scared. Mother Osk says the rot is just the dark being rude.'

k: _(She coughs for a long time.)_
src: '_(She coughs for a long time.)_'

k: Are you the Gloamweaver? Hesk says there's a girl with a black Crest.
src: 'Are you the Gloamweaver? Hesk says there\'s a girl with a black Crest.'

k: Is it scary?
src: 'Is it scary?'

k: It is cold. Sometimes it is lonely.
src: 'It is cold. Sometimes it is lonely.'

k: Mine's going to be Mender, I think. Like Mother Osk. Or the one that gets to ride the boats.
src: 'Mine\'s going to be Mender, I think. Like Mother Osk. Or the one that gets to ride the boats.'

k: I do not know which one that is. I have only had one Crest, and nobody gave it to me.
src: 'I do not know which one that is. I have only had one Crest, and nobody gave it to me.'

k: Do you know the counting rhyme? The Mirefen one?
src: 'Do you know the counting rhyme? The Mirefen one?'

k: "One for the Lantern, two for the light, three for the heron that fishes at night—"
src: '"One for the Lantern, two for the light, three for the heron that fishes at night—"'

k: ...I can't do the rest. It makes me cough.
src: '...I can\'t do the rest. It makes me cough.'

k: Then I will wait, and you will tell me the rest when you can.
src: 'Then I will wait, and you will tell me the rest when you can.'

k: Serve the light, not the man holding the lamp. I'm going to try that for a while. See how it fits.
src: 'Serve the light, not the man holding the lamp. I\'m going to try that for a while. See how it fits.'

k: The Mender brought me the draught herself. Didn't ask whose side I was on.
src: 'The Mender brought me the draught herself. Didn\'t ask whose side I was on.'

k: So here's what I owe you. The Lord-Commander's gone north, to the Stormcrown. His warship's waiting there. Something to do with Skyreach.
src: 'So here\'s what I owe you. The Lord-Commander\'s gone north, to the Stormcrown. His warship\'s waiting there. Something to do with Skyreach.'

k: And he's left pickets on every road between here and there, looking for your black-haired friend.
src: 'And he\'s left pickets on every road between here and there, looking for your black-haired friend.'

k: Take this. Dawnguard issue. It's supposed to keep the dark off you.
src: 'Take this. Dawnguard issue. It\'s supposed to keep the dark off you.'

k: Didn't work for me. Might for you.
src: 'Didn\'t work for me. Might for you.'

k: Will you go back? To them?
src: 'Will you go back? To them?'

k: Don't know. Sir Aldous used to say a Dawnguard serves the light, not the man holding the lamp.
src: 'Don\'t know. Sir Aldous used to say a Dawnguard serves the light, not the man holding the lamp.'

k: Seems to me the man holding the lamp has forgotten that.
src: 'Seems to me the man holding the lamp has forgotten that.'

k: _(quietly)_ He said that to me, too.
src: '_(quietly)_ He said that to me, too.'

k: Garrick's column went north, two days back. Toward the Stormcrown.
src: 'Garrick\'s column went north, two days back. Toward the Stormcrown.'

k: A soldier who can't march is a soldier who can't serve. That's what he said when they left me.
src: 'A soldier who can\'t march is a soldier who can\'t serve. That\'s what he said when they left me.'

k: Don't — don't come closer. I've got the rot.
src: 'Don\'t — don\'t come closer. I\'ve got the rot.'

k: ...Kestrel? Bram Kestrel? The squire who froze at the Trial?
src: '...Kestrel? Bram Kestrel? The squire who froze at the Trial?'

k: That's me.
src: 'That\'s me.'

k: I was in the stands. Third row. You were very... still.
src: 'I was in the stands. Third row. You were very... still.'

k: Yes. I've had notes.
src: 'Yes. I\'ve had notes.'

k: The Lord-Commander's column came through two days ago, limping down off the Greyspine like whipped dogs. I'd caught the fever on the march. They left me where I fell.
src: 'The Lord-Commander\'s column came through two days ago, limping down off the Greyspine like whipped dogs. I\'d caught the fever on the march. They left me where I fell.'

k: Garrick says a soldier who can't march is a soldier who can't serve.
src: 'Garrick says a soldier who can\'t march is a soldier who can\'t serve.'

k: Garrick says a lot of things.
src: 'Garrick says a lot of things.'

k: He says a lot of things about you.
src: 'He says a lot of things about you.'

k: ...I expect he does.
src: '...I expect he does.'

k: Mother Osk says she'll Kindle me by candlelight if she has to. Is that allowed?
src: 'Mother Osk says she\'ll Kindle me by candlelight if she has to. Is that allowed?'

k: She says she doesn't care if it's allowed. I like her a lot.
src: 'She says she doesn\'t care if it\'s allowed. I like her a lot.'

k: I'm sixteen next spring. Mirefen kids get Kindled at our own Lantern.
src: 'I\'m sixteen next spring. Mirefen kids get Kindled at our own Lantern.'

k: If the light doesn't come back... do I just not get a Crest?
src: 'If the light doesn\'t come back... do I just not get a Crest?'

k: I got mine early. From a blind lady in a desert. It's not that great.
src: 'I got mine early. From a blind lady in a desert. It\'s not that great.'

k: ...It's a little bit great.
src: '...It\'s a little bit great.'

k: What if the light gets me wrong?
src: 'What if the light gets me wrong?'

k: Then you tell it so.
src: 'Then you tell it so.'

k: I closed the shutters last night. First time in two winters.
src: 'I closed the shutters last night. First time in two winters.'

k: I slept like a stone. I'd forgotten how.
src: 'I slept like a stone. I\'d forgotten how.'

k: We found this. In the chapel, in the Drownmere.
src: 'We found this. In the chapel, in the Drownmere.'

k: "Always the long way home." He had that put on it as a joke. He was always late for supper.
src: '"Always the long way home." He had that put on it as a joke. He was always late for supper.'

k: He isn't really out there, is he. On the water. It's just the fog, remembering him wrong.
src: 'He isn\'t really out there, is he. On the water. It\'s just the fog, remembering him wrong.'

k: The Gloam remembers things. It does not remember them _right_.
src: 'The Gloam remembers things. It does not remember them _right_.'

k: Then I'll remember him right. That will have to do.
src: 'Then I\'ll remember him right. That will have to do.'

k: She threads the ring onto the string around her neck, and tucks it under her collar, close.
src: 'She threads the ring onto the string around her neck, and tucks it under her collar, close.'

k: Tobin grew these on the roof. Swore they'd make you strong. They never did a thing for him. Maybe you'll have better luck.
src: 'Tobin grew these on the roof. Swore they\'d make you strong. They never did a thing for him. Maybe you\'ll have better luck.'

k: The old chapel in the Drownmere. He always went the long way round, past it. Please — if you see a ring...
src: 'The old chapel in the Drownmere. He always went the long way round, past it. Please — if you see a ring...'

k: Every night, when the fog comes up, my Tobin walks on the water. Out there, past the reeds.
src: 'Every night, when the fog comes up, my Tobin walks on the water. Out there, past the reeds.'

k: He drowned two winters ago. Since the Lantern went dark, he comes back. He doesn't look at me. He just... walks.
src: 'He drowned two winters ago. Since the Lantern went dark, he comes back. He doesn\'t look at me. He just... walks.'
